correctness.rationale: The complete certificate exhaustively covers 3031 nonempty faces by 1469 disjoint incident matched pairs and 93 critical cells, one in dimension zero and 92 in dimension five. All 13846 oriented Hasse covers are checked acyclic by a complete topological sort; Forman discrete Morse therefore gives an integral wedge of 92 five-spheres. The dual is the Alexander dual on 14 vertices and has integral reduced homology rank 92 only in degree six. Its full two-skeleton implies simple connectivity, so Whitehead/Hurewicz yield a wedge of 92 six-spheres. Its 147 ten-vertex facets make it pure nine-dimensional and non-shellable due to homology in degree six. Two independent face predicates and a mod-two boundary reduction check the finite counts, but mod-two data are not used as proof of the integral claim.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches of mathematical findings and published literature, comparison with available earlier claims and targeted inspection of three primary full texts found no theorem giving the fourth robust Heawood homotopy type or its fourth total-cut dual. Published graph-specific third-cut and all-bipartite third-robust results have different robustness parameters. Filakovsky's fourth-level families contain four-cycles and cannot include the girth-six Heawood graph. The 92-sphere count and non-shellability are supported by a new explicit finite Morse certificate, not inferred from previous tables. Residual bibliographic priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The Fano-plane incidence graph is a canonical small cubic bipartite girth-six configuration, excluded from square-sequence fourth-robust calculations. The newly computed level-four homotopy type gives an exact test case of 92 integral five-spheres beyond the established all-bipartite third-level result. The dual yields a pure nine-dimensional non-shellable total-fourth-cut complex with 92 integral six-spheres, an intrinsic topological and shellability classification of a natural associated object.
